biography: Shahid Ziaur Rahman was born on 19 January 1936 at Bagbari in Gabtali of Bogura district. He became one of the major military and political figures in the history of Bangladesh. After receiving his military education, he joined the Pakistan Army and later became involved in the Liberation War of Bangladesh in 1971. During the war he served as a sector commander and later commanded Z Force. He became internationally and nationally known for his role in the early broadcasting of the declaration of independence from Kalurghat on 27 March 1971. After independence he became Chief of Army Staff and later emerged as a major political figure. He became President of Bangladesh in 1977. During his presidency he emphasized agricultural production, rural development, private-sector participation, administrative decentralization and national economic development. He also promoted the idea of greater regional cooperation in South Asia, which later became associated with the formation of SAARC. His political career remains an important and sometimes controversial part of Bangladesh's modern history. His birthplace in Bagbari makes him one of the most prominent political and military personalities associated with Bogura. His wartime service, military leadership and later political activities have made his name an important part of the historical heritage of Bogura and Bangladesh.

name: Muhammad Ali Bogra
majorContributions: Participated in politics before and after the partition of India.

biography: Muhammad Ali Bogra was a prominent politician, diplomat and statesman who was born on 19 October 1909 in Bogra during the period of British India. He came from a politically influential family and became involved in public affairs during the final years of British colonial rule. He entered politics through the Muslim League and later became associated with the political administration of Pakistan after the partition of India in 1947. His diplomatic career was particularly important. He served Pakistan as ambassador in several countries, including Burma, Japan and Canada, and developed experience in international diplomacy before becoming one of Pakistan's senior political leaders. In 1953 he was appointed Prime Minister of Pakistan, a position he held until 1955. During his premiership he became associated with constitutional reform, particularly through the Bogra Formula, which attempted to address representation between East and West Pakistan. His career illustrates the important political role played by people from the Bogura region during the late colonial and early Pakistan periods. Although his political career was conducted largely at the Pakistan level, his birthplace gave Bogura a prominent place in the political history of South Asia. He remains one of the best-known statesmen born in Bogura and an important historical figure for any district-level heritage database.

name: Prafulla Chaki
majorContributions: Participated in the anti-British revolutionary movement.
Participated in armed resistance against British colonial rule.

biography: Prafulla Chaki was a young revolutionary and nationalist who was born on 10 December 1888 in Bihar village of Bogura. He grew up during a period when anti-British political activities were spreading rapidly across Bengal. During his student years he became involved with organizations promoting physical training and nationalist consciousness. He later became associated with revolutionary groups including Jugantar. His name became particularly associated with Khudiram Bose and their attempt to assassinate British magistrate Douglas Kingsford. The attack failed to kill Kingsford and instead resulted in the deaths of two British women. Chaki attempted to escape after the incident but eventually faced capture by the colonial authorities. Rather than surrender, he took his own life. Although his life lasted only a short period, his participation in the revolutionary movement made him a symbolic figure in the history of anti-colonial resistance in Bengal. His birthplace in Bogura is especially significant for the district's historical heritage because he represents one of the earliest generations of young people from the region who became involved in organized resistance against British colonial rule. His story is remembered in the broader history of India's independence movement and in the political history of Bengal.

name: M. R. Akhtar Mukul
majorContributions: Worked for the Mujibnagar Government during the Liberation War.

biography: M. R. Akhtar Mukul was a prominent Bangladeshi journalist, writer, editor and broadcaster who was born on 9 August 1929 in Chingashpur near Mahasthangarh in Bogura. He completed his higher education at the University of Dhaka and developed a long career in journalism and broadcasting. His most important historical contribution came during the Liberation War of Bangladesh in 1971. He became associated with the Mujibnagar Government and worked through broadcasting as part of the wider effort to motivate the people of Bangladesh and communicate the struggle for independence. His radio programme Charampatra became particularly famous for its satirical, emotional and politically powerful presentation of contemporary events. The programme helped maintain morale among the people and fighters and later became an important cultural record of the Liberation War. Mukul also wrote books dealing with Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and the political history of Bangladesh. His career connected journalism, literature, broadcasting and political history. Because he was born in Chingashpur of Bogura, his life forms an important part of the district's literary and cultural heritage. His work is especially valuable for understanding how mass communication was used during the Liberation War.

name: Mustafa Nur-Ul Islam

biography: Mustafa Nur-Ul Islam was an eminent Bangladeshi educationist, writer, journalist and cultural activist who was born on 1 May 1927 in Chingashpur near the historic Mahasthangarh area of Bogura. His father Sa'dat Ali Akhanda was also a writer, and the literary atmosphere of his family influenced his intellectual development. Nur-Ul Islam received higher education from the University of Calcutta, the University of Dhaka and the University of London. He became involved in the Language Movement and later developed a long career as an academic, writer and journalist. During the Liberation War of 1971, while he was in London, he worked to build international awareness and support for the independence struggle of Bangladesh. His academic and cultural activities covered Bengali literature, history, education and public affairs. He was eventually recognized as a National Professor, reflecting the importance of his intellectual contribution to Bangladesh. His career represents the connection between the Language Movement, Bengali cultural identity, education and the Liberation War. His birthplace in Chingashpur makes him one of the notable intellectuals associated with Bogura's cultural heritage. His life is particularly useful for a district heritage database because his contributions were not limited to one profession; instead, he worked across education, literature, journalism and cultural activism.

biography: Khodeja Khatun was a prominent Bangladeshi educationist, writer, poet and social worker who was born on 15 August 1917 in Mandaldharan of Bogura. She belonged to a generation when opportunities for women's higher education were limited, yet she achieved a significant academic career and became one of the notable female educationists of her time. She obtained a Master's degree in Bangla from the University of Dhaka and later served as a professor at Eden Mohila College. She eventually became principal of Government Women's College in Rajshahi. Alongside teaching, she developed a literary career and wrote poetry, essays, stories and works related to Bengali folk literature. One of her important works is Bagurar Loksahitya, which is particularly relevant to the cultural heritage of Bogura because it records aspects of the district's folk traditions. She also served as president of the Bangladesh Women Writers Association and participated in various social and literary organizations. Her achievements were recognized through several awards including the President's Gold Medal in 1967, the Nurunnessa Khatun Vidyabinodini Medal and the Abdur Razzak Memorial Medal. Her life represents the development of women's education, literature and cultural participation in Bangladesh. For Bogura, she is especially important because her work preserved elements of the district's literary and folk heritage.

biography: Bedaruddin Ahmad was a distinguished Bangladeshi singer, musician and music educator who was born on 15 March 1927 in Sherpur of Bogura district. He developed an interest in music at an early age and received training from several respected teachers of classical music. His training included instruction from Gour Chandra Ghosh, Ustad Yusuf Khan Quraishi, Ustad Mohammad Hossain Khasru and Ustad Munshi Raisuddin. He later became associated with radio broadcasting and established himself as a respected singer. After the partition of India he moved to Dhaka and worked as a full-time singer at Radio Pakistan's Dhaka centre. He also played an important role in establishing the Bulbul Lalitakala Academy and eventually served as its principal. Through his teaching and performances he helped develop formal music education in Bangladesh at a time when professional music was not always widely accepted in conservative social environments. He also performed in several countries, helping represent Bengali music internationally. His contribution to music was recognized through the Bangla Academy Award in 1974 and the Ekushey Padak in 1980. His birthplace in Sherpur makes him an important cultural personality of Bogura and a significant figure in the district's musical heritage.

name: Zahidur Rahim
majorContributions: Performed Tagore songs despite restrictions during the 1960s.

biography: Zahidur Rahim was a renowned Bangladeshi singer and important exponent of Rabindra Sangeet who was born in Bogura city. He studied at the University of Dhaka and later received formal music training at Bulbul Lalitakala Academy. His powerful and resonant voice helped establish him as a respected performer of Rabindranath Tagore's songs. He became associated with cultural institutions including Chhayanaut and Bulbul Lalitakala Academy and later worked as a music producer and staff artist at Bangladesh Radio. His career became particularly significant during the 1960s when the Pakistan government attempted to restrict the public performance of Tagore's songs. Zahidur Rahim continued to perform Rabindra Sangeet, making his work part of the wider Bengali cultural movement that contributed to the rise of Bengali nationalism. He performed songs from Tagore's dance dramas including Shyama and Chandalika and helped popularize Amar Sonar Bangla. His cultural activism and musical performances therefore went beyond entertainment and became connected with the preservation of Bengali cultural identity. His birthplace in Bogura city makes him an important cultural personality for the district and an example of Bogura's contribution to the development of modern Bengali music and cultural consciousness.

biography: Romena Afaz was a prominent Bengali novelist and writer who was born in Sherpur of Bogura district in 1926. She became known for her contribution to Bengali popular literature and produced a substantial number of novels. Her literary works include Desher Meye, Kagojer Nouka, Shesh Milan, Aleyar Alo, Jani Tumi Ashbe, Priyar Kontho, Bhul-er Sheshe, Rakte Anka Map, Mandigarh-er Bari, Rongiya, Harano Manik, Husna, Nil Akash and Kundi Bai. Her writing helped establish a popular literary tradition connected with the social and emotional experiences of Bengali readers. The Bogura District Administration lists her among the district's notable writers and specifically identifies Sherpur as her birthplace. Her contribution is important to Bogura's cultural heritage because she represents the literary tradition of the district and demonstrates the participation of women in Bengali popular fiction. biography: Tarun Majumdar was a renowned Bengali film director and writer who was born on 8 January 1931 in Bogra during the period of British India. He later became one of the important filmmakers of Indian Bengali cinema. His career was associated with the filmmaking group Yatrik, through which he worked with other filmmakers before establishing himself as an independent director. He became known for films that focused on Bengali social life, human relationships, rural and middle-class experiences and literary themes. Among his best-known films are Kancher Swarga, Nimantran, Ganadevata and Fuleswari. His cinema combined strong storytelling with detailed observation of Bengali society and culture. He worked extensively with Bengali actors and musicians and contributed to the development of a distinctive Bengali cinematic style. His career lasted for several decades and earned recognition in the Indian film industry. The documented birthplace of Bogra makes him particularly relevant to the cultural heritage of present-day Bogura district, even though most of his professional career was based in India. His inclusion in a Bogura heritage database is valuable because he represents a major contribution from a person born in the region to Bengali cinema beyond the borders of present-day Bangladesh. He died in Kolkata on 4 July 2022.

name: Apu Biswas
majorContributions: Worked as an actress and producer.
biography: Apu Biswas is a Bangladeshi film actress, model and producer who was born in Bogura. She entered the Bangladeshi film industry in the mid-2000s and made her acting debut in Kal Shokale in 2006. She subsequently appeared in numerous commercially successful Bengali films and became particularly well known for her collaborations with actor Shakib Khan. Among her notable films are Koti Takar Kabin, King Khan, No. One Shakib Khan, Ekbar Bol Valobashi, Ek Mon Ek Pran, Chachu Amar Chachu, Devdas, My Name Is Khan, Samraat and Lal Shari. Her role as Parvati in the Bengali adaptation of Devdas was one of the notable performances of her career. She became one of the recognizable faces of Bangladesh's mainstream commercial cinema and maintained a substantial popular following. She later expanded her involvement in the film industry through production work. Her birthplace in Bogura gives the district a connection with one of the best-known contemporary Bangladeshi film actresses. Her career is relevant to a Discover Bogura cultural database because she represents the modern entertainment industry and the participation of Bogura-born personalities in national cinema. His career has included significant Test performances, limited-overs contributions and memorable victories for Bangladesh. He also served as captain of Bangladesh in different formats and became one of the senior leaders of the national dressing room. biography: Nabib Newaj Jibon is a Bangladeshi professional footballer who was born on 17 August 1990 in Shibganj of Bogura district. He began his professional club career with Uttar Baridhara before moving through several domestic clubs and eventually becoming associated with Dhaka Abahani, one of the country's leading football clubs. During his time with Abahani he contributed to several domestic successes, including Bangladesh Premier League titles and cup competitions. He made his senior international debut for Bangladesh in 2015 during a FIFA World Cup qualifying match against Kyrgyzstan and later scored his first international goal against Sri Lanka. His international career established him as one of the notable footballers from Bogura.
